items.q: The sex preponderance written for IgA nephropathy presentation is:
The >50% presentation cluster of IgA nephropathy is adolescents with synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria plus:
opts: Isolated oliguria with a normal urine sediment
items.exp: Adolescents, synpharyngitic, episodic macrohematuria, intervening microhematuria + proteinuria. (Book p773)

items.q: The asymptomatic arm with microhematuria and proteinuria covers what share of IgA patients?
items.exp: 30-40% patients: asymptomatic + microhematuria and proteinuria. (Book p773)

items.q: The 1% RPGN arm of IgA nephropathy is annotated as:
items.exp: 1% patients: RPGN (adult HSP); 5% nephrotic; 5% directly as CKD. (Book p773)

items.q: A 30-year-old has BP 160/100, proteinuria, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL and bilaterally contracted kidneys; biopsy shows mesangial IgA. Which printed arm of IgA nephropathy is this?
opts: The 5% straight-to-CKD arm with a contracted kidney
The >50% adolescent cluster with intervening microhematuria and proteinuria
The 1% RPGN arm annotated as adult Henoch-Schonlein purpura
items.exp: As printed, the presentation list puts 5% directly into chronic kidney disease with hypertension, proteinuria, rising serum creatinine and a contracted kidney; the adolescent cluster with intervening microhematuria and proteinuria is the >50% arm, and crescentic disease is the 1% adult-HSP arm. (Book p773)

items.q: The IgA prognosis rule of 1/3 splits into spontaneous resolution, develop CKD and:
opts: Near normal RFT with stable course
items.exp: 1/3 spontaneous resolution; 1/3 near normal RFT, stable course; 1/3 develop CKD. (Book p773)

items.q: In the MEST-C discussion, mesangial IgA alone carries normal features; the bad-prognosis indicators are IgA deposits outside mesangium (eg. capillary loops), any proliferation other than mesangial and:
opts: Tamm-Horsford protein casts within the tubules
Isolated C3 staining along the capillary loops
items.exp: Bad prognosis: IgA outside mesangium; any non-mesangial proliferation; non IgA deposits (IgG, IgM). (Book p773)

items.q: In the prognostic list on this page, crescents (the RPGN lesion) sit with the bad-prognosis findings.
opts: True — crescents are grouped with the bad-prognosis entries
False — crescents are given no prognostic value at all
False — endocapillary hypercellularity is called chronic and inactive
True — and gross hematuria is listed alongside them as a bad sign
items.exp: Endocapillary hypercellularity → bad prognosis (active disease); segmental sclerosis + tubular atrophy → CKD → bad prognosis; crescents (RPGN) → bad prognosis. (Book p773)

items.q: Among the 'others' prognostic notes, macrohematuria earns a good prognosis because it permits:
items.exp: Macrohematuria: early diagnosis → good prognosis. (Book p773)

items.q: Both serum complement levels and serum IgA are marked on this page as having no value in IgA nephropathy.
opts: True — serum C3/C4 and serum IgA are each followed by 'no value'
False — serum IgA is the recommended screening test
False — a low C3 must be shown before biopsy is considered
True — but the note applies only to children
items.exp: Serum C3/C4 → no value; serum IgA → no value. (Book p773)
